answer: Use credential-anchored identity: each account must anchor itself to credentials from at least three independent issuers, so no single issuer can mint Sybils. At the zenith of trust, a credential is a revocable claim, not a self-chosen name. The signal of legitimacy for an account is the overlap of those attestations, rechecked against revocation lists each epoch. A Sybil attacker must pass three vetting processes and pay their fees for every fake identity, and keep them valid. If any issuer revokes one credential, the account loses standing, so mass forgery collapses at the first audit.
